title: Modi Vows to Serve India's People Until His Last Breath
excerpt: Addressing a public gathering in Banaskantha, Gujarat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked 25 years in public office, credited citizens for his journey, and said he would remain dedicated to serving them until the last moment of his life.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi told a public gathering in Banaskantha, Gujarat, on Friday that he would remain dedicated to serving the people until the very last moment of his life.
  • Modi marked 25 years in public office, saying he first took oath in October 2001 and crediting citizens for entrusting him first with Gujarat and then with the country.
  • At the event he inaugurated and laid foundation stones for development projects worth over Rs 14,000 crore, according to reports of the address.
  • He said his government had shielded farmers from rising global fertiliser prices during tensions in the Gulf and accused critics of spreading rumours about shortages.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said he would continue serving the people of India until his last breath, addressing a public event in Banaskantha district in Gujarat during a visit in which he inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for development projects worth over Rs 14,000 crore.

Speaking at the gathering, Modi framed his time in office as a responsibility handed to him by ordinary citizens. A person from an ordinary family, whose generations had never imagined holding even the position of a village head, was given the opportunity to serve Gujarat and then the entire country, he said, according to an ANI report of the address carried by LatestLY.

"I will continue serving people until my last breath."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India

Twenty-five years in public office

Modi referred to completing 25 years in public office on October 7. He said it felt like only yesterday that he first took the oath of office in October 2001, when, in his words, people showered him with love. Modi became chief minister of Gujarat in October 2001 before leading the Bharatiya Janata Party to national power and becoming prime minister in 2014.

"Service to the people leads to service to the nation, and the development of Gujarat contributes to the development of the country. Whatever I have been able to achieve for the nation, the credit belongs to all my fellow countrymen," he said. He added that he would remain indebted to the people for the rest of his life and dedicated to serving them until its last moment.

Farmers, fertiliser and the Gulf

A large part of the address dealt with agriculture. Modi said his government had protected farmers from a sharp rise in global fertiliser prices during tensions in the Gulf, saying the government had spent heavily so that the burden of higher prices did not fall on farmers. He accused some people of spreading rumours about shortages of fertilisers and gas, saying they wanted to defame him and were happy to see the country in difficulty.

He said Rs 4.5 lakh crore had been transferred to small farmers under the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, and that more than 26 crore soil health cards had been made available to farmers. Agriculture, he said, had been connected with technology, and animal husbandry — in which he credited women with a major role — was an important part of the rural economy.

Banaskantha and the cooperative pitch

Modi praised Banaskantha's contribution to agriculture and the cooperative sector, saying potatoes produced in the region had gained global recognition. He praised Banas Dairy for expanding the cooperative movement beyond Gujarat, including to Kashi, and said an expansion of potato processing capacity would allow larger quantities to be procured, benefiting farmers.

He also spoke about the Cluster Development Programme for fruit and vegetable growers, under which 12 clusters have been approved for crops including tomatoes, potatoes, chillies, grapes, bananas, onions, oranges, pomegranates and cocoa. Two clusters approved for North Gujarat would benefit potato farmers in Banaskantha and Sabarkantha, he said, with support for new orchards and rejuvenation of existing ones.

What the remarks signal

The Banaskantha address combined a personal pledge about his own future with a defence of his government's record on farm support. A detailed account of the speech and its top quotes was also published by 7Globe. Modi offered no change in course: the message from Gujarat was that the prime minister, 25 years after first taking office in the state, intends to keep serving in public life and to keep the government's pitch to farmers at the centre of that case.
